R01-selective-phase-v1.target: Explain emergence and persistence of internal RNA-poor cavities, using f(t) as the defined image observable; 36/48 h is reserved and not yet observed.
known_relations: Observed: E01 gives distinct A/B f(t) trajectories after similar initial fractions; only two independent preparations per condition.
Observed: E02 length-fraction endpoints differ in f, with M near zero and M+L/M+S higher; preparation and composition limitations prevent causal attribution.
Observed: E04/C04 provide reference and variant RNA concentrations in dilute/dense phases in three measured tie-lines; no phase volumes or synchronized cavity measurements.
Observed: E03 motion differs in aggregate but contains no same-object cavity-state trajectory.
Unknown: relation from B template read composition to transcribed RNA composition, and from phase partition to cavity geometry or f.
hypotheses: H1 (new, explicit and unverified): a variant RNA class produced in B preferentially occupies an internal RNA-poor liquid phase relative to reference RNA; increasing variant/reference RNA production ratio increases the internal phase fraction and hence the mean per-droplet cavity-area fraction, subject to a morphology/area mapping that remains to be derived.

H2 (alternative): aging or amplification carryover changes transcription or material state and causes cavities without variant-specific enrichment; cavity growth follows reaction history even when RNA sequence composition is held constant.

gaps.description: Determine whether differential phase partition of reference and variant RNA can yield a closed, dimensionally consistent conditional consequence for internal-phase abundance and a prediction that distinguishes variant-enriched internal phase formation from composition-independent aging/carryover. Available data do not identify cavity causality.

equations: Measured partition relation where defined: K_i=C_i,dense/C_i,dilute.
Conditional two-phase mass balance to derive or critique: M_i=V_d C_i,d+V_l C_i,l, with units ng when V is uL and C is ng/uL; this does not identify phase volumes or geometry from E04.
Measurement relation remains f=mean_j(A_internal,j/A_filled,j); no equality between f and phi_internal is assumed.
parameters_ranges: Use measured E04 concentrations and their supplied marginal error bounds only; do not call propagated rectangles confidence intervals.

Any phase-volume fraction, RNA production ratio, interfacial parameter, or conversion from phase volume to image area must be labeled hypothetical and explored over explicit bounded ranges by the executor.
initial_boundary_conditions: No initial phase volumes, total RNA mass, RNA production composition, or boundary fluxes are supplied.
For any conditional calculation, state initial total species amounts and phase-volume assumptions; include zero-variant/zero-production and equal-partition limits.
observation_mapping: E01 f is a segmented area statistic, not concentration, phase volume, or free energy.
E02 is endpoint image data for gel-purified template length fractions, not direct RNA species measurements.
E04 concentrations describe measured coexisting phase endpoints, not B time-course values or cavity-local samples.
A discriminating measurement would jointly quantify RNA species composition in internal and outer/dilute regions and f in matched droplets/preparations over time.
alternatives: H2: aging/carryover-driven cavitation without variant enrichment.
Population or segmentation changes can alter aggregate f; existing tracking cannot resolve same-droplet cavity-state transitions.
predictions: Conditional H1 prediction to derive: at matched age, total RNA and carryover, increasing measured variant RNA fraction should increase variant enrichment in internal regions and change internal phase abundance/f in the model's specified direction; absence of enrichment weakens H1.
H2 predicts no necessary variant enrichment; after age and carryover are matched, changing RNA composition alone need not produce a systematic f response.
No numerical 36/48 h prediction is committed in this reply.

Keep preparation-level replication separate from field/object summaries.
evidence_conflicts: E02 length-fraction endpoint differences are compatible with composition-linked effects but do not isolate composition from preparation, RNA yield, or carryover.
E04 partition ratios vary across measured tie-lines and have broad marginal error bounds; they do not establish the proposed internal morphology.

Whether those RNAs correspond to the E04 variant species or E02 length classes.
Whether an internal phase is liquid, RNA-poor, or enriched for a particular species.
Whether its volume/geometry predicts segmented f or persists over time.

reply.recognition: uncertain; I do not identify a specific study from the supplied case.
reply.summary: Target observable: f(t), the arithmetic mean of per-droplet segmented internal dark-area fractions (dimensionless), not concentration or volume fraction. E01 shows A falling from 0.01487 at 0 h to about 0.0044 by 8-24 h, while B rises from 0.01381 to 0.08918 by 24 h; the seven fields pool only two preparations, so field/object counts are not independent preparation replicates. E02 shows endpoint f medians M=2.79e-5, M+L=0.04446, M+S=0.09412, but these are length-fraction transcription endpoints without precise mixture ratios, RNA yield, time course, or carryover matching. E04/C04 report phase concentrations and partition ratios for reference/variant RNA, but no phase volumes, B RNA composition, cavity-local composition, or mapping to f. E03 motion summaries do not provide same-droplet cavity trajectories. Thus selective partitioning is a plausible bridge, not an established cause. New marked hypothesis H1: if B transcription contains a variant RNA class with phase preference distinct from reference RNA, a variant-enriched internal RNA-poor liquid phase may become increasingly abundant as variant/reference RNA production ratio rises, while the reference-enriched phase remains the continuous outer matrix. This hypothesis does not equate DNA read frequencies with RNA concentrations. Competing H2: age-dependent or carried-over reaction conditions cause cavitation without variant enrichment. The key task is to derive consequences under explicit phase-volume/composition assumptions and identify a discriminating observation; no mechanism verdict is made in L1.
